High-level answers up-front:
- We publish supported P50/P95 commitments for the Hosted API for common routes; those depend on model family and region. Samir / Naomi — technical details below so you have something concrete to review. I'll call out where the SLA vs operational artifact splits.

1) Measurement semantics (recommended):
- Per-region, per-route rolling 5-minute window sample aggregation.
- For each 5-minute window we compute request-level latencies, then derive P50 and P95 from that window; SLA compliance is evaluated by counting 5-minute windows where P95 exceeds the contractual threshold.
- We define a monthly allowance: SLA is considered met if no more than X% of 5-minute windows exceed the P95 threshold across the billing month (we can discuss the % floor; default hosted is 0.5%).

Rationale: 5-minute rolling windows smooth out transient microbursts while preserving visibility into sustained latency degradations. Shorter windows (1m) are noisy for multi-tenant hosted runs; longer windows (15m+) mask customer-visible spikes.

2) Ramp / exception policy (proposal):
- If FinleyTech schedules a coordinated ramp window (documented start/end) we will:
  a) Exclude the specified ramp windows from SLA calculations for up to 21 days.
  b) Apply model-variant fallback and rate-aware routing with a documented capacity plan — we will provide a capacity buffer estimate and recommended throttling/backoff knobs you should implement client-side.
  c) During the ramp we will run an elevated telemetry cadence and set up a dedicated Ops channel for real-time mitigation.

3) Fallbacks and compatible model variants:
- When capacity is constrained we can route low-priority or latency-tolerant requests to quantized or cheaper model variants automatically; these are transparent at the API layer as long as you accept a modeled quality delta.

Open items for commercial: define P50/P95 thresholds (numeric), define allowed % of violating windows, and sign-off on the 21-day max exception.

-Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

- Ramp exception: up to 21 calendar days exclusion if the ramp window is scheduled at least 7 days in advance, with weekly Ops check-ins during the ramp.
